description: We are OUTSTRIP, a Nicaraguan team tackling Field Shift by turning NASA Earth data into practical crop-rotation insights for farmers. Our strengths include industrial engineering, sustainability, research, problem-solving, design, and communication. We’re looking for teammates skilled in Python, web development, GIS, data analysis, AI, or agriculture who want to build a practical solution with real impact.
summary:
StarStep is an interactive, bilingual (English/Spanish) space-archaeology web game that reframes legacy spaceflight hardware left off-Earth not as technological debris, but as active scientific witnesses to planetary history. Addressing the "NASA's Discarded Equipment: Storytelling" challenge, players step into a Cadet suit alongside floating AI companion Lito to retrace two landmark missions separated by 35 years: Apollo 11 on Mare Tranquillitatis (1969) and the Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity across Meridiani Planum (2004–2018).

Built as a zero-server, offline-ready HTML5 Single-Page Application (2,071 lines of clean HTML5/CSS3/ES6+ JavaScript), StarStep runs smoothly on modest school computers without internet or backend installations. Every dialogue card and polaroid separates empirical telemetry from game fiction using live OBSERVED, INTERPRETED, and NARRATIVE badges, integrating 25 curated NASA multimedia assets and official NASA Science 3D models. By transforming static archives into hands-on scientific inquiry, StarStep equips classrooms across Latin America and worldwide to teach authentic planetary science.
details:
Overview & Core Concept

Conventional space outreach celebrates rocket launches and first footprints while overlooking what happens to scientific hardware after live broadcasts fade. StarStep — Chapter 1: Rock & Roll turns this misconception into a playable investigative expedition built around one unifying scientific question: "What do rocks tell us about water?" Players explore how human field geology on the Moon (Apollo 11) and remote robotic sensing on Mars (Opportunity) follow the exact same five-step scientific method.

How It Works (Gameplay & Pedagogical Flow)

  • Historical Context & Cadet Hub: After a 10-slide spaceflight chronicle (1957–1969), players create a local Cadet profile (with SHA-256 PIN protection, 6 custom avatars, and 4 suit palettes) or enter directly via a 15-scene Demo Mode designed for rapid judge walkthroughs.
  • Act I — The Moon (Apollo 11, July 1969): Strictly honoring mission history, Apollo 11 carried no lunar rover. Players explore on foot within a 100 m radius of Eagle under a compressed 135-minute O₂ timer, collecting 5 real geological samples (including vesicular basalt 10057 and regolith 10084), deploying the 48 kg EASEP package and LRRR retroreflector on a top-down 5 m coordinate grid aligned at 0° toward Earth, and analyzing basalt 10057 under a Houston lab microscope.
  • Act II — Mars (MER-B Opportunity, 2004–2018): Following a 26-airbag-bounce landing into Eagle Crater, players traverse three genuine geological sites (Eagle Crater, Homestake, and Esperance), rationally pairing 2 of 6 real NASA instruments (Pancam, Mini-TES, Microscopic Imager, RAT, APXS, Mössbauer) to uncover hematite "blueberries," gypsum veins, and neutral-pH smectite clays, culminating in the June 2018 global dust storm blackout (=10.8) after 45.16 km driven.
  • Act III — Mirror Synthesis & Explorer Certificate: Players match 6 left-behind artifacts to their scientific discoveries, compare both missions side-by-side in a 5-step Mirror Scientific Method matrix, browse a 6-tab Collection Logbook containing 23 verified NASA assets, and export a custom 1600×1132 px PNG Explorer Certificate.

Epistemological Rigor & Creativity (The Tripartite Filter)

To prevent edutainment from blurring facts with fiction, every dialogue box and polaroid inside StarStep displays a live color-coded epistemological badge:

  1. OBSERVED (Cyan): Primary NASA photography (AS11-*, PIA*), NSSDCA catalog IDs (1969-059C / -04), and direct spectrometer telemetry.
  2. INTERPRETED (Amber): Peer-reviewed geological inferences (such as the 3.63 Ga cooling age of basalt 10057 or ancient liquid water geochemistry on Mars).
  3. NARRATIVE (Purple): Transparently declared creative licenses (the 24-second arcade launch sequence, hovering companion Lito, and compressed O₂ gameplay timer).

Technical Architecture & Tools Used

  • Zero-Server Standalone SPA: Engineered in 2,071 lines of dependency-free HTML5, CSS3, and ES6+ Vanilla JavaScript. It launches instantly from a local folder or static host with zero Python/SQL servers, no external databases, and no heavy WebGL requirements.
  • Audiovisual & Accessibility Stack: Native 320×180 px HTML5 Canvas 2D pixel-art rendering (image-rendering: pixelated), procedural chiptune audio synthesized in real time via the Web Audio API, live English/Spanish instant language switching (ES/EN), built-in Web Speech API text-to-speech narration, prefers-reduced-motion support, and client persistence via localStorage + Web Crypto API (SHA-256).
  • NASA 3D & Media Integration: Incorporates 25 bundled local NASA multimedia files (22 JPEGs and 3 MP4s, including oppy3d.mp4 and two narrated pre-descent briefings with English subtitles) modeled after official NASA Science 3D .GLB/.USDZ spacecraft geometry.

Intended Impact & Scalability

Across classrooms in Nicaragua and Latin America—where planetary labs are scarce and internet bandwidth is often uneven—StarStep provides teachers, astronomy clubs, and universities with a zero-barrier, offline-capable STEM workshop. Its modular architecture already prepares future chapters: Chapter 2: Wheels and Dust (Apollo LRV, Curiosity, Perseverance) and Chapter 3: Distant Signals (Pioneer, Voyager, and the Golden Record).
